reason: The bent antenna seems like the immediate obstacle to getting the radio working, and a service tool could straighten or repair it.
expectation: I expect a usable antenna or a step toward repairing it; I don't know whether the tool alone will suffice.

alternatives.reason: Insulation for the window also seems urgent, but I want to restore communications first.

effect: The antenna is straightened, so I can try mounting it for the radio.
reaction: That repair was straightforward and matched my expectation.
reason: The radio mount is the natural place to install the antenna.
expectation: I expect the antenna to be mounted and perhaps the radio to work, though it may need power too.

effect: The radio works and the delayed message establishes contact; I can turn to preparing the cabin for night.
reaction: The twelve-minute-old voice makes the distance feel tangible, and I want to know what comes next.
reason: Foil and felt seem like useful layers for insulating the window.
expectation: I expect an insulating panel or blanket for the window, although it might need a mounting part.

alternatives.reason: Charging the emergency battery also seems useful for night, but the window is explicitly losing heat.

effect: The materials made quilt stock, which can now be fitted at the window.
reaction: The result is sensible, though the name stock suggests more assembly may be needed.
reason: The window is losing heat, so I will put the reflective quilt there.
expectation: I expect a window covering or an intermediate assembly that reduces heat loss.

effect: The quilt is made, and the spare rail can now be combined with it.
reaction: I expected a further fitting; the rail makes sense as a way to hang it.
reason: I want to secure the quilt at the window with the rail.
expectation: I expect a hung or operable window quilt that helps retain cabin heat.

effect: The sliding quilt addresses the window, but the night goal remains open, suggesting the battery still needs attention.
reaction: The cold easing and the view returning in the morning made the construction feel useful and lived-in.
reason: Charging the emergency battery is the only offered gameplay action and seems useful for a night reserve.
expectation: I expect the array to charge the battery and possibly complete the night preparation goal.

effect: Charging the battery completed the night preparation, and the fuel-cell backup explains how essential systems can persist through darkness.
reaction: The link back to the recovered array makes the reserve feel connected to the earlier work; the fuel cell was a useful detail.

mostWorthwhile.text: Hanging the sliding window quilt was most worthwhile: the physical relief from cold and the promise of a view in the morning made the repair feel like making a home.

leastWorthwhile.text: Making quilt stock and then a window quilt felt like two fairly thin intermediate steps; neither result explained much on its own.

surprise.text: The twelve-minute-old recorded voice made the delay between Mars and Earth tangible, and the fuel-cell backup added a detail I had not anticipated.

arbitrary.text: No action felt entirely arbitrary, though turning quilt stock into a window quilt at the window left me unsure exactly what physical work happened.

continue.text: Yes. The delayed message and small domestic details made me curious about the expedition, although I would hope future combinations offer more decisions or explanation than the quilt intermediates.
